title: Desktop UI v1
goal: Arrange and mix by hand in the Electron app, and review and approve an agent plan visually.
prerequisites: M3 (done): protocol and plans. M0 Electron shell: m0-electron-shell is merged (PR #47); M0 itself stays in progress on m0-macos-bundle, which M5 does not need.

docs/harness/follow-ups.md, section Before M5: taken into the wave 1 and 2 features m5-plugin-registry, m5-shell-hardening, m5-engine-sessions-devices and m5-clap-editor-window below (decided by Fable, delegated by the maintainer, 2026-11-09: the hardening is built by the same TDD, verify and land loop as every feature, and the UI features depend on it). The third-party restart test (from PR #62) lands in its own PR beside them and is not a prerequisite.

humanGates.text: Choose the frontend framework (React or Svelte) at the start of M5, as the spec requires.
humanGates.how: The plan phase presents a short comparison; the maintainer decides. Needed before m5-read-model and the UI features; the wave 1 hardening features (m5-plugin-registry, m5-shell-hardening, m5-engine-sessions-devices) and m5-clap-editor-window do not need it and can run first as a subset.
humanGates.resolution: Decided by Fable, delegated by the maintainer, 2026-11-09 (ADR-0019). React 19 with react-dom, bundled by esbuild and type-checked by the existing strict tsc build. The read model stays framework-free TypeScript (immutable snapshots keyed by revision, unit-tested with node --test) that React reads through useSyncExternalStore; timeline, waveform and meter surfaces are imperative Canvas/WebGL classes and no meter value passes through React state. Strongest reasons: agent authoring reliability, a toolchain that fits app/ as it stands, and an external revision-keyed store that matches React's store contract. m5-read-model adds the pinned dependencies; this PR adds none.

humanGates.text: Review timeline, mixer and plan review usability.
humanGates.how: The maintainer uses the app and lists required changes before the exit check.

humanGates.text: Review the retaken screenshot tour of the redesigned shell in English, Traditional Chinese and Simplified Chinese.
humanGates.how: The maintainer reads the tour PNGs per locale (states 01-25) on Windows and macOS and lists required changes; this is the form the existing ux-review gate takes for the redesign, and it comes before the M5 exit check.

humanGates.text: Confirm the Chinese terminology of the proposal's glossary (section 6.5) against Cubase's Chinese interface.
humanGates.how: The maintainer compares the glossary with a Cubase running in Chinese and corrects the catalogs; needed before m5-ui-i18n is declared done, not before it starts.

humanGates.text: Approve the document change for locators (a singleton entity or a field on root) and whether cycle on/off is restored on open.
humanGates.how: The plan phase of m5-ui-engine-loop-click presents both shapes with the migration each needs; the maintainer or the delegated reviewer decides before implementation.
humanGates.resolution: Decided by Fable, delegated by the maintainer, 2026-11-13: a singleton locators entity (revisioned, undoable, restored on open), per the redesign spec section 7, E-1.

features.title: Plugins load through a registry of approved installs, never from a path the document names
acceptance: A host::PluginRegistry (siann-host-api, a header-only value type) holds installs keyed by {format, path}, each {uid: string|null, name, approved}; uid is known once the install has been probed. The engine host fills it at launch from PluginHost::scan's paths over the platform's standard plugin directories and every --plugin-dir <dir> (repeatable), each carrying the uid, name and approval the JSON file --plugin-registry <file> holds for that path (the shell passes <userData>/plugin-registry.json; the tests a temporary file); nothing is probed at launch, and reading and writing the file lives in native/apps/engine. Every load goes through the registry (PluginInstanceTable::sync, RenderInstanceSet, EngineHost::instantiate): a slot resolves by {format, uid} to the approved installs with that uid; one is it, between several the slot's path chooses (otherwise plugin_not_registered naming the ambiguity), none is plugin_not_registered; descriptorOf passes the resolved install's path, never slot.path. Test: a document whose slot names siann_test_plugin's uid with the path of an unscanned copy loads the registered install; a document naming an unknown uid and the path of a real library never opens that library (a test plugin that writes a marker file when its entry point runs proves it) and the slot is missing with error code plugin_not_registered, its stateBlob kept.

An install loads only when approved: a registered, unapproved install leaves the slot missing with plugin_not_approved. plugin.registry {} returns {plugins: [{format, path, uid, name, approved}]} and plugin.approve {format, path, approved} sets and persists the flag, taking effect at the next instantiate or relaunch: approving an unprobed install probes it with scanPath (running its code is the user's choice at that moment), records uid and name, and answers the PluginError code (plugin_not_found, plugin_load_failed) leaving it unapproved when the probe fails; approved: false needs no probe. Both go through the command thread, honour expectedRevision and the idempotency cache, are in engine.capabilities' methods and are written as Protocol v0 item 21 in the spec and in docs/schemas/protocol-plugins-v0.md; neither is an MCP tool (an agent must not choose what code loads). plugin_not_registered and plugin_not_approved are new stable codes. plugin.instantiate with descriptor {format, path} needs a registered install at that path (job failed, plugin_not_registered, message unregistered_path) that is approved (plugin_not_approved); with {format, uid} and no path, exactly one approved install. The tests that load siann_test_plugin and siann_hostile_plugin pass their build directory as --plugin-dir and approve them through the method.

A path is refused where it enters, before any library opens: a UNC path (\\server\share or //server/share), a path inside the session bundle, and a path that is not a registered install's path. plugin.instantiate answers invalid_params for a UNC path or a path inside the bundle, plugin.insert (a pure command, no bundle in reach) rejects a UNC path with invalid_params, and at load the instance table ignores a refused (unc_path, inside_bundle) or unknown (unregistered_path) hint, never opening it: the slot still loads the uid's single approved install, and only when no approved install exists is it missing with plugin_not_registered, whose message names the hint's reason; a --plugin-dir on a UNC path or inside the bundle is a usage error at launch. Test for each refused form in the command, protocol and playback tests.

blobPath accepts only sha256: followed by exactly 64 lowercase hex digits and otherwise throws host::PluginError("bad_state"), which loadPlugin reports as the slot's error, so sha256:../../x never names a file; the check is model::isStateBlobHash, which the document parser and plugin.instantiate already apply. Tests: blobPath on sha256:../../x, 63 digits, uppercase hex and a bare hash; loadPlugin on a slot carrying such a blob reports bad_state and reads nothing outside <bundle>/blobs.

features.title: The shell holds one instance and ends every engine: single-instance lock, permission denial, ready timeout, no devtools, wedged-quit e2e
acceptance: main.ts calls app.requestSingleInstanceLock() before whenReady and quits at once when the lock is not granted; the holder focuses its window on second-instance. Playwright e2e: a second launch of the app (child_process) exits 0 without spawning an engine (one engine pid, no second ready line) and the first window is focused.

The supervisor fails a launch that writes no ready line within readyTimeoutMs (default 30 s; SIANN_SHELL_READY_MS overrides; the injected schedule times it) the way it fails a malformed one: protocol-error with the reason, SIGTERM, SIGKILL after killGraceMs, restart under the backoff. Unit tests with the injected scheduler: the timeout fires; the ready line, an exit and stop() each cancel it.

failLaunch ends the child's stdin before SIGTERM; a kill() that returns false or throws (SIGTERM or SIGKILL) is recorded in the launch's stderr lines, and the child counts as exited only when its exit event arrives or killGraceMs runs out, never earlier. Unit tests for a false return and a throw on each signal.

session.defaultSession.setPermissionRequestHandler and setPermissionCheckHandler deny every permission for every origin, and setDevicePermissionHandler denies every device. Playwright e2e: navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia({audio: true}) rejects with NotAllowedError, Notification.requestPermission() resolves denied, and navigator.permissions.query({name: 'notifications'}) reports denied.

Menu.setApplicationMenu installs a menu with no toggleDevTools, reload or forceReload role and the window has webPreferences.devTools false, unless SIANN_SHELL_DEVTOOLS=1; before-input-event swallows F12, Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+I, Ctrl/Cmd+R and F5. The menu does not depend on app.isPackaged, so the e2e proves the packaged build too. Playwright e2e: Menu.getApplicationMenu() holds none of those roles, F12 and Ctrl+Shift+I leave webContents.isDevToolsOpened() false, and Ctrl+R leaves the renderer's connection count unchanged.

Unit tests cover the paths PR #47 left untested: a ready line arriving during stop() (no ready event, stop() still ends the child), start() twice (one spawn), stderr trimmed to stderrLines with a partial last line, each field of the ready line's strictness (schema, port range, token and mcpToken hex and their distinctness, sessionId form, pid, about), and a CRLF ready line; the e2e covers setWindowOpenHandler denying window.open and will-navigate blocking a URL outside siann://app/ while allowing one under it.
supervisor-process.test.ts stops the supervisor (await supervisor.stop()) in every test's finally before reaping, so a give-up regression fails the test at its deadline instead of hanging the runner.

Playwright e2e of the bounded quit on a wedged engine: the engine takes the test-only option --test-wedge (ignores stdin EOF and SIGTERM, a usage error without SIANN_SHELL_TEST=1's SIANN_ENGINE_TEST_ARGS path), the shell's graces are set short through SIANN_SHELL_STOP_GRACE_MS and SIANN_SHELL_KILL_GRACE_MS, and quitting the app returns within stopGraceMs + killGraceMs + 2 s, exits 0 and leaves the engine pid gone.

features.title: The engine lists and selects devices, opens and locks sessions, reloads repaired media, and exposes transport and status to MCP
acceptance: engine.devices {} returns {devices: [{id, type, name, isDefault, current}]}, id as --device takes it (fake on every build, <type>/<name> on a SIANN_WITH_JUCE build) from the enumeration siann-cli play lists; engine.select_device {id} stops and closes the running device, opens the named one on the main thread's tick path (stopped at the playhead, counters from zero, retried under the device backoff as a reopen is) and returns engine.status's device object, or not_found for an unknown id (the current device plays on) and device_open_failed when the open fails (engine.status then shows deviceError and the retries continue). Both go through the command thread, honour expectedRevision and the idempotency cache, are in engine.capabilities' methods, and are written as Protocol v0 item 22 in the spec and in docs/schemas. Tests (launch tests): a core-only engine lists fake; launched without a device, selecting fake makes transport.play advance the playhead; selecting nope answers not_found and the device plays on; a selected fake device under --fake-open-failures shows device_open_failed, then recovers.

MCP tools wrap the transport and status methods one to one (Protocol v0 item 14): play, stop, locate, engine_status and list_devices in the propose scope, select_device in the trusted scope; docs/schemas/protocol-mcp-v0.md lists them with their schemas. MCP adapter tests: each tool reaches its method with the same params, result and error codes (no_device included), and a propose client calling select_device gets the scope error.

session.open works in siann-engine: ServerOptions::openSession rebinds the EngineHost (its playback engine, auditioner and meter publisher) to the opened session while the device stays open, and the next session.sync carries the new sessionId and head. Launch test: open a second bundle, session.sync shows its sessionId and documentHash, transport.play plays it, and the first bundle's lock is released.

The engine locks the bundle it serves: Session::open and Session::create take <bundle>/lock exclusively (O_EXCL, CREATE_NEW) holding {pid, startedAt}, release it on close and at exit, and take over a lock whose pid is dead. A second engine on a locked bundle exits 1 with the session_locked launch error (Protocol v0 item 17), and session.open on a locked bundle answers session_locked. Tests: session tests (a second open fails, a dead-pid lock is taken over, close releases) and a launch test with two engines on one bundle, the second exiting 1 with session_locked and a third launching once the first has exited.

A session served with deviceError because its first graph could not be built (media_missing and the other media codes in Process model) builds and plays again once a commit no longer needs the missing file: EngineHost retries the graph on every new head while deviceError names a media code, with no relaunch. Launch test: a bundle whose media file was removed launches with deviceError.code media_missing; command.execute removing the clip that names it clears deviceError and transport.play advances.

features.title: Frontend read model keyed by revision
acceptance: The renderer holds a read model keyed by revision, applies session.changed deltas, recovers with session.sync, and is optimistic only for continuous gestures.

features.title: CLAP editor windows on the desktop target
acceptance: siann-host-desktop supplies the window: an EditorWindowFactory in siann-host-api that ClapPluginHost takes at construction (none in the headless target) creates a top-level native window on the main thread (owned by --owner-window through GWLP_HWNDPARENT on Windows; floating at NSFloatingWindowLevel with FullScreenAuxiliary on macOS; a plain X11 window on Linux, as the JUCE editors are) and hands back its native handle. ClapPluginHost::openEditor runs the gui extension's is_api_supported, create (the platform API, not floating), set_parent, get_size and show on the main thread and sizes the window to the plugin; closeEditor runs hide and destroy; the host's resize_hints_changed and request_resize callbacks resize the window. capabilities().editor is true only when the gui extension supports the platform API; without a factory openEditor still throws editor_failed.

plugin.open_editor on a CLAP slot of a SIANN_WITH_JUCE engine returns {editorOpen: true, nativeHandle}, plugin.close_editor closes it, and a window closed from its title bar leaves editorOpen false in the next result; the headless engine keeps editor_failed. The spec's Protocol v0 item 19 and docs/schemas/protocol-plugins-v0.md drop the 'until siann-host-desktop supplies a window' clause.

siann_test_plugin's CLAP build gains a gui extension (win32, cocoa and x11 child views drawing a flat colour, no toolkit) so CI proves it: the desktop engine tests open and close its editor, and editor.spec.ts gets a CLAP case proving GWLP_HWNDPARENT ownership on Windows. On the maintainer's machine SIANN_TEST_CLAP names Surge XT's .clap for the same test (SKIP naming the variable when unset, FAIL on a missing path), and the macos-hands-on gate in M0.json adds opening a CLAP editor to its checks.

features.title: Timeline with Canvas/WebGL waveforms and clips
acceptance: Clips render from peak pyramids; place, move, trim and remove issue commands; Playwright tests cover each command path. Placing a clip chooses a media entity of the document; importing a file from the UI is not part of m5-timeline (no media.import protocol method exists yet; follow-ups).

features.title: Mixer with faders, pan, mute, solo and meters
acceptance: Fader gestures use the parameter channel with leases; one revision per gesture end; meters from binary frames.

features.title: Plan review UI
acceptance: Diff of a plan against the current revision, audition of the branch, approve, reject and partial approve.

features.title: English, Traditional Chinese and Simplified Chinese: message catalogs, locale detection and switch, localized formatters and plan wording
acceptance: app/src/renderer/i18n holds one typed catalog per locale (en, zh-Hant, zh-Hans); en defines the key type, so tsc fails on a missing or extra key in another catalog.

A unit test walks the renderer's .ts and .tsx sources with the TypeScript compiler API and fails on JSX text, on string literals and on the literal text of template literals in title, aria-label, placeholder and alt and in the first argument of fillText, outside an allow-list of fixed symbols (M, S, R, W, e, dB, L/C/R).

A unit test fails when a catalog value is empty, drops a placeholder the English message has, equals the English value without being allow-listed, or uses a character of the other Chinese script from the test's pair table.
A unit test maps system language tags to locales: zh-TW, zh-HK, zh-MO and zh-Hant-* give zh-Hant; zh-CN, zh-SG, zh-Hans-* and zh give zh-Hans; everything else gives en.

e2e: with the system language reported as zh-TW the first launch renders in Traditional Chinese and <html lang> is zh-TW; the manual switch changes every visible string without a reload and the choice survives an app restart.

Plan step descriptions, toast messages, engine error codes and relative times are built from the catalogs in all three locales (unit tests per locale; an engine error keeps its code in front, and in English shows the engine's own message, with the catalog text only when it sent none, as UI redesign 6.2 says); dB values, pan values, positions and the letters M and S are byte-identical across locales.
e2e fit check at 1440x900 and 1024x700 in en, zh-Hant, zh-Hans and a pseudo-locale that pads English by 40 %: no labelled control has scrollWidth greater than clientWidth.

ux-tour.spec.ts takes SIANN_UX_LOCALE and writes its states into one folder per locale. Tour states changed: in en, 01-22 gain only the language switch in the status panel (no English wording, order or other layout changes); adds the zh-Hant and zh-Hans sets of 01-22. The en set moves to <SIANN_UX_OUT>/en/.

features.title: Engine and protocol: locators as a revisioned document entity, cycle playback and a metronome
specRefs: siann-command (pure C++) — the core of SIANN
acceptance: A command session.set_locators {left, right} (audio-domain frames as decimal strings, left < right, otherwise invalid_locators) changes the session's locators through command.execute: one revision, journaled, published by session.changed, and one session.undo restores the previous pair.
A session saved with locators and reopened reports the same pair; the document format version is bumped with a migration for bundles that have none.
A plan step may set the locators; plan.preview returns the entity with before and after.
transport.set_cycle {enabled} makes playback wrap from the right locator to the left: a 4-bar cycle plays 100 passes on the fake device and nulls against the same audio laid end to end.

transport.set_click {enabled, gainMilliDb?} adds a click generated from the tempo map to the device output only: it is on the beat within one sample across a tempo change, and a render started with the click on contains no click.

Cycle and click state are in the results of the transport methods and in engine.status; a second connection receives transport.changed when either changes and session.changed when the locators change.
engine.capabilities lists the methods and features.locators, features.cycle and features.click; MCP tools wrap transport.set_cycle and transport.set_click one to one in the propose scope.
Setting cycle or click creates no revision. Tour states changed: none (no UI).

features.title: Design tokens, bundled fonts, Cubase-style zones with draggable and collapsible boundaries, the key-command layer and the status bar
acceptance: At 1440x900 and 1024x700 the document never scrolls (e2e asserts documentElement.scrollHeight equals clientHeight); each zone scrolls internally.

The three zone boundaries of the proposal's section 2.3 (left zone / project zone, project zone / lower zone, project zone / right zone) each drag within their stated range, collapse below their minimum and restore, and work from the keyboard: reached by real key presses from its zone (Tab inside a zone walks its controls and divider), arrow keys 8 px, Shift 32 px, Home and End the minimum and maximum, Enter restores the default; double-click restores the default (e2e per boundary, no element.focus() from script).

Zone sizes, collapsed states and active tabs are stored under one localStorage key, survive an app restart, are unchanged when a different session is opened, and no protocol request carries them (e2e inspects the request log).

The project zone cannot be hidden. Ctrl+Alt+L and Alt+I toggle the left zone, Ctrl+Alt+E and Ctrl+Alt+B the lower zone, Alt+F3 and F3 show the lower zone on the MixConsole tab, and hide it when it is already showing that tab, Ctrl+Alt+R toggles the right zone, Ctrl+Alt+P shows the right zone on the Plans tab; Tab and Shift+Tab move a visible focus frame between zones from a zone or the page and between a zone's controls from inside it (wrapping there, Escape back to the zone, Enter into it); F6 and Shift+F6 move it from anywhere.

Key commands come from one preset table (Cubase): a unit test finds no duplicate binding within a zone scope, the dispatcher sends a key to the focused zone first, and no command fires while a text field has focus.
A control whose method is absent from engine.capabilities is not in the DOM (unit test on the capability selector with a reduced capabilities fixture).

The status bar shows the name, version, commit, licence and source URL from engine.about: a unit test renders both AGPL-3.0-or-later and GPL-2.0-or-later, and another finds no licence literal in renderer source.
Only index.tsx references window.siann (unit test), and the built bundle renders its disconnected state in a plain Chromium tab without an exception (e2e outside Electron).
Inter and JetBrains Mono load from local files with their OFL texts beside them; the CSP has no remote font or style source.
Tour states changed: 01-22 (every state gets the new shell); the review reads 01, 02, 03 and 05.

features.title: Disconnected and reconnected states
acceptance: While the engine is disconnected a full-width banner shows, every zone is dimmed and inert, and no control sends a request (e2e on the crash scenario counts requests).
On reconnect a toast names the recovered revision and the selection is cleared.
Tour states changed: 21, 22.

features.title: Track list and event display: two-layer surface, split ruler, info line, zoom and scroll by Cubase's keys and wheel
acceptance: A fixed track list shows colour, number, name, M, S, gain in dB, pan as L/C/R and a mini meter per track; clips are never drawn under it; double-click renames (track.rename) and the T key, the + button above the track list or a double-click on the track list's empty space adds a track (track.add) with a client-chosen id trk_<16 hex> (as clip ids), channels 2 and the catalog's default track name with the next free number.
The canvas follows its container's size and the device pixel ratio; the ruler shows bars and beats with subdivisions that adapt to zoom.

H and G, Ctrl+wheel and a vertical drag in the lower half of the ruler zoom horizontally and keep the position under the pointer or cursor fixed (H and G zoom about the project cursor when it is in view and about the view's centre otherwise); Shift+H and Shift+G and Ctrl+Shift+wheel change track heights; Shift+F shows the whole session; Shift+wheel scrolls horizontally; none of them scrolls the page.
Dragging a track's lower border changes its height, and Ctrl-drag changes all tracks.
A frame in which only the project cursor moved does not redraw the content layer (counter in the test hook).
The info line shows the selected clip's start, end, length, offset and gain in user units, read-only.
A selected clip has a 2 px outline; a drag shows a tooltip with the new position and the delta; clip move, trim, place and delete still commit exactly one revision each.
Muted tracks and tracks muted by another track's solo are dimmed; an empty session shows guidance text.
The track list / event display boundary drags within 140-420 px, never collapses, moves with the arrow keys and restores 216 px on double-click; its size is stored in siann.layout.v1.
Tour states changed: 01-22 (every state shows the project zone since m5-ui-shell); the review reads 01, 02, 06, 07, 10, 11, 12.

features.title: MixConsole in the lower zone and Inspector basics: Cubase strip layout, +6 dB fader, value-control modifiers, one meter canvas
acceptance: Strips are in track order with, top to bottom: pan, M and S, fader with meter, level and peak values, name on the track colour; a meter-only master strip is fed by the legend's master entry.
The fader runs from minus infinity to +6 dB with 0 dB at 75 % of its travel (unit test on the taper); a stored gain above +6 dB pins the cap at the top and shows the true value.
Ctrl-click sets a fader to 0.0 dB or a pan to C in one revision; Shift-drag is fine adjustment; double-clicking a value accepts a typed value; these hold for every value control in the app.
A fader gesture still commits one revision at its end, a fader held still keeps its lease, and a tooltip shows the value while dragging.

All meters are drawn on one canvas at display rate with zero React commits while playing (profiler count in the e2e); peak hold decays as specified, a clip indication latches, and clicking the peak value resets it.
Values read as dB with one decimal and an explicit sign, and pan as L35, C, R40; no milli-dB or internal pan unit is visible.
The Inspector's Track tab shows the selected track's name, colour, M, S, volume and pan and always agrees with that track's strip.
Tour states changed: 04, 07, 08, 09.

features.title: Plans tab in the right zone: cards, user wording, state-valid actions, audition banner
acceptance: Each plan is a card with its first step, step count, relative time, state badge and short hash; steps are numbered from 1 in user wording with select all and none.
No milli-dB value, internal pan unit or entity id is visible unless a per-row disclosure is opened.
Only the actions valid in the plan's state are shown, with one filled primary (unit test on the action set per state).

Approve and apply sends plan.approve then plan.apply; when the second is refused the plan stays approved and the refusal is shown. Audition sends plan.approve, plan.propose and audition.hear and the card reads approved for audition (unit test with a refusal at each position).
While audition.changed reports a branch, a banner naming the plan is visible from the event display and the MixConsole, and the hearing switch shows the side heard.
A stale plan shows a stale badge with the reason in user units and its approve action is disabled; a partially approved parent is labelled split from parentPlan; a rejection shows its reason.
A new plan raises a toast and the count on the Plans button without taking focus.
Tour states changed: 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18, 19, 20.

features.title: Transport bar and project cursor: Cubase transport keys with laptop fallbacks, time display, auto-scroll, undo and redo
acceptance: Space starts and stops, numpad Enter starts, Num 0 stops, Num . and the comma key go to the project start; none fires while a text field has focus.
The project cursor is drawn on the overlay layer and the position display updates at display rate with zero React commits.
A click in the lower half of the ruler locates, also while stopped; Shift+P accepts a typed position.
The display shows Bars+Beats and Seconds, the period key exchanges primary and secondary, and at 120 BPM it reads 3.1.000 at 4 s (unit test across a tempo change).
With auto-scroll on (F) the view pages when the cursor leaves it during playback and does not move while a clip is being dragged.
Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Shift+Z call session.undo and session.redo; a refusal is shown as a toast.
With no audio device the transport controls are disabled and their tooltip gives the reason.
Tour states changed: 04, and the top bar in every state.

features.title: Editing by Cubase's gestures: select and split tools, Alt-drag copy, duplicate, split at cursor, corner resize, clip gain, snap and grid
acceptance: Keys 1 and 3 choose the Object Selection and Split tools; with the selection tool Alt-click splits and Alt-drag copies; Ctrl-drag constrains a move to one axis.
Alt+X splits the selected clips at the cursor, or every clip under the cursor when nothing is selected; Ctrl+D places a copy of the selection directly after it, several clips as one unit.
Each of these operations is one command.execute and one revision, and one undo restores the previous state (e2e per operation).

Splitting a clip with a non-zero source offset yields two clips whose audio is continuous: the right piece's sourceStart equals the left piece's sourceStart plus its length (unit test on the command builder).
A clip resizes from its lower corners; holding Ctrl ignores snap; the volume control at the clip's bottom left changes clip gain in one revision with Shift for fine steps.
J toggles snap; with snap type Grid and grid type Bar a dragged clip lands on bar lines; Beat and Adapt to Zoom change the step as specified (unit tests on the snap maths).
Shift-click adds to the selection and Ctrl+A selects all; L moves the cursor to the selection start, N and B to the next and previous clip; Alt+S zooms to the selection.
M and S toggle mute and solo on the selected track; Shift+Delete removes the selected tracks after a confirmation.
Tour states changed: 10, 11, 12; appends 25 (clip split and duplicated).

features.title: Locators, cycle and metronome in the UI
acceptance: Dragging in the upper half of the ruler draws the locator range and sends one session.set_locators on release; Ctrl-click and Alt-click set the left and right locator; dragging the range moves it; Ctrl+Z restores the previous range.
Clicking the range, the cycle button, Num / or the slash key toggles cycle; the band is light when cycle is on and grey when off, with a tint over the tracks.
P sets the locators to the selection and Alt+P also turns cycle on and starts playback; Num 1 and Num 2, and Shift+1 and Shift+2, move the cursor to the locators.
The metronome button and C toggle the click; a right-click gives its level.
The band and both buttons always show the engine's state, including a change by another connection, an undo, or an applied plan (e2e with a second client).
Reopening the session shows the same locator range.
Against an engine whose capabilities lack the methods none of these controls is in the DOM and no request is sent (e2e with a reduced capabilities fixture).
Tour states changed: none of 01-22; appends 23 (locators set, cycle on) and 24 (metronome on).

exit.how: Playwright scenario plus the maintainer's UX review (human gate).

exit.text: Review and approve an agent plan visually.
exit.how: Playwright scenario with an MCP-submitted plan.
